_comment: Machine-readable form of the SP1 syscall ABI modelled by
checked against the Lean source by scripts/check-sp1-pin.sh.
'words' counts 64-bit doublewords (SP1 v6 memory cells are u64).
'arg1'/'arg2' name the register holding each operand pointer; every
modelled precompile writes its result in place at the arg1 block.
'accel' names the RiscvZkvm.Rv64.Accel function the id maps onto -- these
are the concrete functions ZiskAccel.lean already defines and tests, so no
new cryptography is introduced by the SP1 backend.

'hint' lists SP1's input-path syscalls. They are host syscalls rather than accelerators, but unlike the 'host' entries they are NOT handled by Execution.step -- step has no arm for either id, so delegating them would silently no-op the only way an SP1 guest can read input.

modelled.name: UINT256_MUL
modelled.note: a1 holds y then modulus contiguously; result written at a0. modulus 0 TRAPS, matching ZiskAccel's Arith256Mod stance -- the pinned executor source does not fix that case, and Accel.arith256Mod is documented as requiring callers to guard m != 0.

_vendor_comment: NOT upstream SP1. These ids come from the dmpierre/sp1 fork, which adds a
Pallas precompile for Zcash Orchard work, and they do not exist in the
revision PROVENANCE.toml pins. They are pinned in their own class so that
check-sp1-pin.sh cannot be read as claiming otherwise.
They need no new mathematics: Pallas is y^2 = x^3 + 5, so a = 0, and
Accel.curveAdd/curveDbl are parameterised by the prime and already assume
a = 0. Only the modulus is new. The operand layout is identical to
SECP256K1_ADD/DOUBLE -- 8 dwords at a0, 8 at a1, result in place at a0.
_commit_comment: SP1's COMMIT shares id 0x10 with the zkvm-standards write_output that
Execution.step implements, but the two are unrelated: COMMIT takes
(index, word) in a0/a1 and writes a public-values digest word, while
write_output takes (ptr, size) and copies bytes out of memory. Under the
sp1 backend StepOn.sp1Ecall handles it before the host delegation is
reached; under zisk the id keeps its write_output meaning inside step.
Reading one as the other is not a near miss -- a real guest's digest word

commit.name: COMMIT
commit.note: a0 = digest index, a1 = digest word; appended to MachineState.committed

commit.name: COMMIT_DEFERRED_PROOFS
commit.note: no-op in the pinned executor; eight sites immediately before every guest's HALT. NOT folded in with VERIFY_SP1_PROOF (0x1B), which keeps trapping.

host.name: read_input
host.note: zkvm-standards C ABI; not an SP1 syscall id

_not_modelled._comment: Every id below TRAPS under the sp1 backend rather than no-opping, matching ZiskAccel.lean's stance on unmodelled CSR ids. Reasons are recorded so a future change knows what is missing versus what is deliberate.
_not_modelled.SHA_EXTEND / SHA_COMPRESS: SP1 splits SHA-256 into message-schedule expansion and 64-round compression; Accel.sha256Compress does both as one function, so the decomposition does not line up. Accel.sha256W (ZiskAccel.lean:254) already computes the 64-word schedule and is the natural basis for SHA_EXTEND in a follow-up.
_not_modelled.*_FP_ADD / FP_SUB / FP_MUL: Base-field (non-Fp2) add and sub have no counterpart in the Accel namespace.
_not_modelled.ED_ADD / ED_DECOMPRESS / *_DECOMPRESS: Edwards curves and point decompression need a modular square root, which Accel does not provide.
_not_modelled.SECP256R1_*: The P-256 base field is not among Accel's pinned primes.
_not_modelled.U256XU2048_MUL / UINT256_ADD_CARRY / UIN: Carry-propagating and 2048-bit variants have no Accel counterpart. Plain UINT256_MUL *is* modelled (see above); these are its wider siblings.
_not_modelled.POSEIDON2 / MPROTECT / SIG_RETURN / ENTE: Prover-infrastructure syscalls, not arithmetic precompiles. HINT_LEN/HINT_READ used to be lumped in here, which was wrong: they are SP1's input path, and they are now modelled -- see the "hint" section above.

hint.name: HINT_LEN
hint.note: Front hint vector's byte length in t0, or u64::MAX when the input stream is empty. Does not consume. The guest branches on the sentinel: li a0,-1; ecall; beq t0,a0,...

hint.name: HINT_READ
hint.arg2: length (must equal the front vector's length)
hint.note: Pops the front vector and writes it at a0 as LE doublewords. Extent is len/8 + 1 doublewords: SP1 writes a final zero-padded word unconditionally, even when len is a multiple of 8. Traps on exhausted stream, length mismatch, or misaligned a0 -- all three are assert!/panic! in the executor.
